Hey @Cynabuns,

Thanks for discussing this Markdown thumbnail issue with me. After our discussion I had a bit more of a think about it and came up with a solution. I've documented the solution here and created a prototype of the video post gallery here, in my development environment.

Thanks for the kick up the butt!

:-)

HERE'S MY SOLUTION

I ended up satisfying my needs in a very specific way that may not suit everyone.

I wanted to create a gallery of clickable images, with a clickable description below to indicate to the user if they've already visited the URL based on the link's color, that each linked to a specific YouTube video (or post comment, not sure witch at this stage).

Solution: Create a Discussion post with a normal Markdown table with three columns in the message area. Fill the table with linked description for a single video. Now, edit the stylesheet to apply a separate style for each cell in that table, using the nth-child operator to create a pseudo element that is inserted before the link. Style the pseudo element to be an image of a standard side and it will automatically inherit the link properties and be clickable.

You can see my prototype thumbnail video gallery here.

Here's an example of the Markdown and CSS for a table with three columns and two row:

(add this markdown to the message area of your new discussion post)

--- |--- |--- |
[Link A](www.a.com)|[Link B](www.b.com)|[Link C](www.c.com)|
[Link D](www.d.com)|[Link E](www.e.com)|[Link F](www.f.com)|

(now customize the CSS to style those table links with inserted pseudo images)

.md tr:nth-child(1) td:nth-child(1) a:before {content:""; display: inline-block; background-size: 232px 182px; width: 232px; height: 182px; background-image: url(www.images/a.jpg);}
.md tr:nth-child(1) td:nth-child(2) a:before {content:""; display: inline-block; background-size: 232px 182px; width: 232px; height: 182px; background-image: url(www.images/b.jpg);}
.md tr:nth-child(1) td:nth-child(3) a:before {content:""; display: inline-block; background-size: 232px 182px; width: 232px; height: 182px; background-image: url(www.images/c.jpg);}
.md tr:nth-child(2) td:nth-child(1) a:before {content:""; display: inline-block; background-size: 232px 182px; width: 232px; height: 182px; background-image: url(www.images/d.jpg);}
.md tr:nth-child(2) td:nth-child(2) a:before {content:""; display: inline-block; background-size: 232px 182px; width: 232px; height: 182px; background-image: url(www.images/e.jpg);}
.md tr:nth-child(2) td:nth-child(3) a:before {content:""; display: inline-block; background-size: 232px 182px; width: 232px; height: 182px; background-image: url(www.images/f.jpg);}

Issues with this solution

If anyone tries to create a description post that contains a table with links in it, everything will go to shit and their table will be full of surprise thumbnails. You do have an option to style your tables to have no borders or backcolor and then create two or three empty, essentially invisible tables before the one you intended to display your content, and then use the nth-child to reference the third table within the message area of the description... this will allow most people to create at least a couple table containing links before they get surprises... however I chose not to worry about such issues because it would only complicate my solution and the risk of people creating discussion posts with tables that contain links seemed relatively acceptable to me.

This can now be marked as resolved, as far as I am concerned.
